title: Dictation safety timings are shared rules with tests
was: The 1 second dead-man, the 3 second stall limit, the 3 second settle window, the 3 second alarm and the 1 second standing-check grace were plain values inside the app, and no test would fail if one changed.
changed: Those values and the decisions that use them moved into the shared, tested rules; the app now asks those rules, and a new rule allows a start press only once the safety record was written.
now: Not read back: no Swift toolchain could be installed in this session, so the build and the tests have not run on the change.
doneWhenEvidence: Timing tests: DictationSafetyRulesTests pins 1 s dead-man, 3 s stall, 3 s settle, 3 s alarm, 1 s grace, plus each boundary just under and at it; not yet run.
App calls rules: git grep finds none of heartbeatTimeout, axStallLimit, settleWindow, escalateAfter or the 1.0 grace in Sources/Ensemble; each use now names DictationRules.
Fails first: not shown; swift could not be installed here, so no red run was seen.
Written before pressed: noPressUnlessTheSafetyRecordWasWritten pins that a refusal, including a failed record write, permits no press; the start path calls pressPermitted; not yet run.
Asserts changed: none; DictationSafetyRulesTests.swift only gains tests.

Dictation safety: record-before-press, dead-man (greater than 1 s), standing check (grace greater than 1 s, settle at least 3 s), alarm (at least 3 s) and send rules keep the same values and comparisons, now pinned.

Checks: swift build could not run; swift test --filter DictationSafetyRulesTests could not run; full swift test could not run; scripts/bundle.sh and check-size not needed (no weight added). Review by hand: every comparison kept its strictness (heartbeat and stall greater than, grace greater than, escalate and settle at least); the stall property is now read on every tick, not only during a hold, and it is a cheap in-memory read. Choices made without asking: the once-a-second cadence (every 4th 0.25 s tick) stays in the app because it is how often the timer runs, not a threshold; log text now prints the constants instead of literal 1 s and 3 s, which reads the same. The press rule also takes the called-off flag, since that is the same branch in the start path. No docs or counts needed updating; docs/safety.md wording is unchanged.
memory: Sources/EnsembleCore/DictationRules.swift now owns every dictation safety timing; Sources/Ensemble/Claude/DictationSafety.swift only reads clocks and CoreAudio and passes elapsed seconds in.
